units.title: Fwd: H&S winter bulletin
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, forwarding the safety team's winter bulletin, which goes to every site. The short version: - No lone working at the edges of a site after the light goes. - Head counts at the end of each shift. - Warm-up breaks every two hours in hard frost. - Report any slips on ice, however small. None of this is new; they just like it in writing each December. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the safety team have also asked every site lead to confirm by return that the bulletin has been read. I appreciate you can't reply from site, so I've told them you'll confirm in Friday's numbers note, which I've also told them is perfectly normal for island jobs. One less thing. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Period 3: roster check reminder
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Reminder. A roster check for period 3 is due before period close. The system will compare the active site roster with daily timesheets from days 15 to 24 and flag any day with a missing entry. Flagged days are not paid until resolved. You do not need to take any action unless you receive a further notice. Reference GLS-RC-P3. This address cannot receive replies.

units.title: A small correction
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. Forgive the extra email. In yesterday's piece I described the camp lights as being near the island's northern end, based on what people in Gilliver told me. A reader on Lisle has written to say they look further west from there. If I've got the geography wrong, I'm sorry; it isn't my intention to point at anyone. I've asked the desk to soften it online. Nell

units.title: Office cover this weekend
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the office is closed at the weekend as usual. If anything urgent comes up on site, the duty phone is on and I'll have it on Saturday. For anything involving anyone's safety, call the Coastguard first and us second; they are quicker than we are and they know the water. I'd rather you never needed either number. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Creel boats welcome calm after a stormy fortnight
units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver's small fleet of creel boats is expected to have its best week of the season as the forecast calm settles over the Sound. After last week's storm kept most boats in harbour for four days, fishermen said they were looking forward to flat water, even at minus three. 'You can't feel your hands, but you can work the whole line,' said one.

units.author: courier
units.text: Prices for brown crab have held up well this month, though lobster has dipped as restaurants in Port Ammet report a quiet run-up to the festive season. Diesel at the harbour pump has risen four cents since the storm. The chandlery said demand for gloves, hand warmers and deck grit had 'gone through the roof'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The harbourmaster reminded crews that the Gilliver Ledge buoy is reported unlit and that the inner basin may ice in the coming nights. Boats leaving before dawn should carry working lights and a radio, she said, and let someone ashore know when they expect to be back.

units.title: Lisle pier: lighting hours extended
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. While the reduced night timetable is in place, the Lisle and Gilliver pier lights will remain on until 23:30 each night, rather than switching off after the last arrival. This is to help passengers making their own way home. Pier staff will lock the waiting rooms at the usual times.

units.title: Portable generator safety
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op safety notice. If you use a portable generator during a power cut: never run it indoors, in a garage or near an open window; never connect it to your home's wiring unless an approved changeover switch has been fitted by an electrician. Back-feeding the network can kill line workers who believe the line is dead.

units.title: The politest caller of the year
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: between calls: a man rang the utilities line at 01:40 to report that his streetlight was out. I said that's the council, not us. He said he knew that, but the council was closed, and he just wanted to tell someone, because it's the only light on his road and his wife walks the dog at six. I logged it anyway. I'll pass it on. sometimes the job is just being the someone.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Hana, that's lovely. I hope the council sort it. Six in the morning with a dog on an unlit road is no fun; I do it here with a head torch and Mo pulling toward every hedge. Tell your supervisor you deserve a biscuit.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: my supervisor says biscuits are 'a wellbeing initiative' and are only available on the second Tuesday. I'm going to email the council's out-of-hours address myself at the end of shift. it's not my job. it's a streetlight. it'll take two minutes.

units.title: Patrol log, still night
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: 00:00 patrol, gate 7 to bay 22. Wind nil. Water like oil. 00:40 reefer alarm on bay 9, reset, unit cycling normally. 01:15 fox by the weighbridge, ignored me. 02:00 new camera on bay 14 checked, clear picture, nothing at the edge. Logged: quiet. Posting because people only post the strange nights, and this is what most nights are.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Thank you. I'd like a whole board of logs like this. Reefer alarms and foxes. Housekeeping suggestion for anyone who wants it: post your quiet nights too. It helps the rest of us remember what normal looks like.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: quiet night log from aisle 41: picked 1,604 items, dropped one jar of pickle (intact), argued with a pallet jack, lost. scanner beeped at me 2,000 times. nobody stood anywhere they shouldn't. the canteen ran out of beans at 01:30. that's the only horror I have to report

units.title: Brackwater Arms quiz went ahead by candlelight.
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Not about the lines, before anyone starts. The Arms quiz went ahead last night by candlelight when the power went at quarter past eleven, landlord read the picture round out loud, describing each photo, which took longer than the rest of the quiz put together. Linesmen came last because we got called out at question 31. Rematch requested.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Estate team won, for the record, by two points. The landlord's description of a picture of a famous bridge as 'a long thing over some water' is the reason. Come back when you've not got a call-out and we'll beat you properly.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: I was on the team that came second and I'd like to raise a formal objection to the 'long thing over some water' question. Half the Sound is a long thing over some water. We put 'the ferry'. We stand by it.

units.title: Bread delivery and a kindness
units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I wish to thank whoever left a bag of grit outside my door on 7 yesterday evening with a note saying 'for your front step, Irena'. I do not have a front step, I live on the seventh floor, but I was very touched and have used it on the path by the bins. My husband would have laughed. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: it was me. i panicked in Hassan's and bought too much salt and thought 'irena' and then didn't think any further than that. glad it went on the bins path. that path is the actual cardio of doom this week

units.title: Cold snap driving, old hand tips
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Minus fifteen out here tonight, so a few tips for anyone driving nights in the cold: fill up at half a tank, not empty. Keep a blanket and a candle in a tin in the cab. If you pull over to rest, pull in somewhere lit, with other trucks. Don't sit on a dark shoulder with your engine running. And stretch every two hours, your back will thank you.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Adding: if you've got a dog in the cab, bring their water inside the cab with you or it freezes. And check paws for salt when you stop. Merle, you said Thursday, the kettle's on here from midnight if you want a cup. Mo will interrogate you.
